title: What's in the Box
about: Meet the parts inside a laptop and a phone, and what each one does.

cards.sentence: This is the laptop's **battery**: it stores the energy that runs everything.
This is the **battery connector**: unplug it, and nothing inside gets power.

cards.title: Before we open anything
cards.body:
Everything you open here is a **simulation**, so tap away.

Real devices are different: **leave opening them to a repair shop**. It can break parts or end the [[warranty]], and a damaged battery can **catch fire**.

cards.prompt: Open it: **screws**, then the **panel**, then **unplug the battery**.

actions.nudge: The panel won't lift until all four screws are out.

cards.explanation: Screws first, then the panel. Then repairers **unplug the battery** before they touch any other part, so nothing gets a jolt of power while they work. (Real laptops often have more screws, and clips too.)
cards.hint: The panel is held on by the screws, and the battery connector only shows once the panel is off.

cards.sentence: This is the **motherboard**: every part plugs into it, and its thin lines carry signals between them.
This is the **CPU**, the brain: it follows the instructions that make your apps work.

cards.prompt: Tap the stick with a row of chips.
cards.sentence: This is **RAM**, a fast workspace that holds the apps you have open right now.
This is **storage** (an SSD): it keeps your photos, apps and files, even with the power off.

cards.prompt: Put each job on its part.
cards.explanation: The small shiny chip, the **CPU**, follows instructions. The **RAM** stick holds open apps, the long **SSD** keeps your files, and the **battery** stores energy. This laptop's RAM and SSD unclip, but many thin laptops have them **soldered** to the board instead.
cards.hint: Use the clues: a small shiny chip, a stick with a row of chips, a long card with stripes, and a lightning bolt.
cards.nudge: Look at the shapes again. RAM is the stick with a row of chips; storage is the longer, narrower card with stripes.

cards.title: Here's a real one

photo.alt: A real laptop with its bottom cover off: a round fan and a curved black heat pipe at the top, a long narrow SSD card in the middle, and a wide battery across the bottom.

cards.caption: A **Framework Laptop 13**, cover off. Can you spot the SSD and the battery?

cards.prompt: A phone packs the same jobs into less space. **Tap each part.**

parts.job: The processor does the CPU's job, and the graphics too, in one chip.
The RAM chip is soldered on, so it can't be swapped.
The storage chip keeps your photos and apps when the phone is off.
The battery fills most of the phone, so it can last all day.
The battery connector is unplugged first in every repair.
The camera's lens looks out through the back cover.
The charging port is open to the outside, so pocket fluff can get in.

cards.explanation: Same jobs as the laptop, packed tighter: the processor, [[RAM]] and [[storage]] chips are all soldered to one small board, so none of them can be swapped. The battery takes up most of the space.

cards.prompt: You can unclip a phone's RAM and swap it, like a laptop's RAM stick.
cards.explanation: **False.** A phone's RAM and storage chips are **soldered** to its board, so they can't be unclipped or swapped.
cards.hint: Think back to the phone's RAM chip. How was it fixed to the board?
cards.nudge: Look back at what the phone's RAM chip said about how it's attached.

cards.prompt: Before touching anything inside, repairers unplug the ___.

options.nudge: The camera doesn't power anything. Which part sends power to every other part?
Storage keeps your files, but it doesn't power anything. Which part does?

cards.explanation: The **battery** goes first. Once it's unplugged, nothing inside has power, so no part gets a jolt while it's worked on.
cards.hint: Which part sends power to everything else?
cards.nudge: Think about which part powers the whole device. Cutting that off first keeps every part safe.

cards.prompt: This phone is **glued shut**. Open it and **unplug the battery**.

actions.nudge: Soften the glue on the back cover first.
The glue is still hard. Soften it first.
Take the back cover off first.
Lift the bracket off the connector first.

cards.explanation: Glue, back, bracket, battery. (In a real phone, two tiny screws hold that bracket down; here they're already out.) The battery is **unplugged first**, before anything else is touched. Repair shops do this with special tools and training, because a damaged phone battery can catch fire.
cards.hint: The back won't lift until its glue is soft. The battery connector is hidden under a small bracket.
cards.safety: **Heating or prying a phone can damage its battery and start a fire.** Repair shops use special tools and training, so never try it at home.

cards.prompt: Tap where your **photos** stay when the phone is off.
cards.explanation: Photos live in **storage**, which keeps everything when the power is off. The camera only takes them, and RAM only holds what's open right now.
cards.hint: Your photos have to survive the phone being switched off. Which part keeps things when the power goes?
cards.nudge: The camera takes photos, but it doesn't keep them. Which part keeps your files when the phone is off?

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Phones and laptops share the same main parts.
- The CPU follows instructions, RAM holds what's open, storage keeps files.
- Repairers **unplug the battery first**. Leave real devices to them.

Next: why RAM and storage are so different.
